sources.title: Aghor Medicine: Pollution, Death, and Healing in Northern India
limitations: Ethnographic and medical-anthropological research does not test an omnipresent consciousness field.
Descriptions of healing practice do not establish paranormal efficacy.
The studied settings and lineages must not be generalized to every Aghori practitioner.

sources.title: Aghoreshwar Bhagawan Ram and the Aghor Tradition
limitations: A dissertation focused on Aghoreshwar Bhagawan Ram and a modern Aghor lineage.
Lineage-specific findings must not be generalized to all Aghoris.
Anthropological interpretation is not experimental evidence of metaphysical claims.

sources.title: The politics of heterodoxy and the Kina Rami ascetics of Banaras
limitations: Repository access provides metadata and abstract-level context; full text is access-limited.
Historical and political analysis does not establish consciousness-field ontology.
Kina Rami history must not be treated as a universal account of Aghor.

sources.title: The Gift of Life: Death As Teacher in the Aghori Sect
limitations: Interpretive and transpersonal scholarship is not prospective evidence of post-mortem survival.
Discussion of death and nonduality does not establish reincarnation or persistent meta-awareness.
The article must not be used to authenticate metaphysical ontology.

bounded_claims.text: Academic ethnographic research documents Aghor approaches to pollution, death, healing, stigma and the interaction of ritual, Ayurveda and biomedicine in studied settings.
bounded_claims.uncertainty: This does not establish paranormal healing, a consciousness field or universal applicability.

bounded_claims.text: A detailed anthropology dissertation provides lineage-specific context for Aghoreshwar Bhagawan Ram and modern Aghor reform, service and practice.
bounded_claims.uncertainty: Its interpretations require lineage-aware reading and cannot represent every Aghori.

bounded_claims.text: A religion dissertation situates Kina Rami ascetics within the history and politics of heterodox Śaivism.
bounded_claims.uncertainty: Full-text review remains blocked by access limits; only bounded bibliographic and abstract-level use is allowed.

bounded_claims.text: A transpersonal-studies article interprets death, nonduality and transformation within an Aghori context.
bounded_claims.uncertainty: The interpretation does not demonstrate survival, reincarnation, persistent meta-awareness or a universal consciousness field.

research_horizon: Lineage-led qualitative research on meanings of nonduality, love, Śiva-consciousness and non-rejection.
Prospective phenomenology of fear of death, disgust processing and self-boundary experience before and after sustained practice.
Behavioural assessment of compassion, service and non-rejection without reducing practice to laboratory constructs.
Physiological or neural measures may study practice-related states but cannot alone adjudicate metaphysical ontology.
